title: Treasury Laws Amendment (2019 Petroleum Resource Rent Tax Reforms No. 1) Bill 2019
short_title: Treasury Laws Amendment (2019 Petroleum Resource Rent Tax Reforms No. 1) Bill 2019

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would change petroleum resource rent tax by lowering the uplift applied to some unused deductions and removing onshore petroleum projects from its coverage.
It would change how carried-forward general and exploration expenses grow before being deducted, with separate rules for older expenditure and amounts transferred between projects.
The reforms would apply from 1 July 2019, while existing projects would retain their current general expenditure uplift unless the new project rules apply.
changes: For new projects, the premium above the long-term bond rate for general expenditure would end after the specified ten-year period.
New or transferred exploration expenses would eventually use a gross domestic product factor instead of a premium above the bond rate.
The Resources Minister could combine related projects only following an application from relevant participants.
summary.affected: Petroleum project participants with carried-forward expenditure and operators of onshore petroleum projects are affected.

speeches.speaker: Matt Thistlethwaite
speeches.brief: Labor supported the Treasury Laws Amendment (2019 Petroleum Resource Rent Tax Reforms No. 1) Bill 2019, which lowers uplift rates on carry-forward expenditure and removes onshore petroleum projects from the PRRT, but moved an amendment calling on the government to also act on multinational tax loopholes and tax havens.

speeches.speaker: Stuart Robert
speeches.brief: The Treasury Laws Amendment (2019 Petroleum Resource Rent Tax Reforms No. 1) Bill 2019 lowers the uplift rate on exploration expenditure to prevent excessive deduction compounding and removes onshore projects from the PRRT to stop transfer of deductions to offshore projects, strengthening tax integrity and ensuring a fairer return for Australia's oil and gas resources.
